llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly checks for /home/user/project.code-workspace existence — the correct filename VS Code produces when saving a workspace named 'project'.
Getter reads /home/user/.config/Code/User/settings.json and extracts editor.wordWrap — the standard user-level settings path on Linux for VS Code.
Metric applies clean partial credit (0.5 + 0.5) covering both sub-goals of the chained instruction.
Negative control resistance is adequate: the workspace file does not pre-exist in setup, and user settings are not pre-seeded with wordWrap=on.

Minor coverage gap: evaluator only checks user-level settings; if an agent sets wordWrap in workspace-level settings (/home/user/project/.vscode/settings.json), this would not be detected. However, 'VS Code editor settings' conventionally refers to user settings accessed via File > Preferences > Settings, so the approach is semantically appropriate.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider also checking workspace-level settings (/home/user/project/.vscode/settings.json) for editor.wordWrap as a fallback, so agents that set it at workspace scope also receive credit.
